glossary.Myocardial ischaemia: Heart muscle not getting enough oxygen-rich blood for its needs.
glossary.Infarction: Death of tissue because its blood supply has been cut off.
glossary.Coronary arteries: The arteries on the heart's surface that supply the heart muscle.
glossary.Lumen: The open channel inside a blood vessel.
glossary.Hyperlipidaemia: High levels of fats such as cholesterol in the blood.
glossary.Angina: Chest pain from heart muscle ischaemia, usually on exertion.
glossary.Constricting pain: A tight, squeezing or band-like pain.
glossary.Exertion: Physical effort, such as walking uphill or climbing stairs.
glossary.Palpitations: An unpleasant awareness of your own heartbeat.
glossary.Heart failure: The heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs.
glossary.Plaque rupture: A crack in an atherosclerotic plaque that exposes its core and triggers a clot.
glossary.Proximal: Nearer the start of the artery, so a block there affects more muscle.
glossary.Stenosis: Abnormal narrowing of a vessel or valve.
glossary.Critical stenosis: A narrowing tight enough to threaten blood flow even at rest.
glossary.Inverted T wave: A T wave pointing downwards on the ECG, a sign of ischaemia.
glossary.Cardiac MRI: A detailed magnetic scan of the heart showing muscle, scar and movement.
glossary.Anterior axillary line: A vertical line down from the front fold of the armpit.
glossary.Mid-axillary line: A vertical line down from the middle of the armpit.
glossary.Limb leads: ECG electrodes placed on the arms and legs.
glossary.Chest leads: The six ECG electrodes V1 to V6 placed across the chest.
glossary.MI: Myocardial infarction: a heart attack, where heart muscle dies from a blocked artery.
glossary.Antiplatelet: A drug that stops platelets sticking together to form clots, such as aspirin.
glossary.Aspirin: An antiplatelet drug that reduces clotting on coronary plaques.
glossary.Statin: A drug that lowers LDL cholesterol and stabilises plaques.
glossary.Beta-blocker: Drug that blocks adrenaline's beta receptors, slowing the heart and lowering its oxygen use.
glossary.Atenolol: A beta-blocker used for angina and hypertension.
glossary.Sexual dysfunction: Problems with sexual desire or function, such as erectile dysfunction.
glossary.CCB: Calcium channel blocker: relaxes arteries or slows the heart, depending on type.
glossary.Asthma: Reversible narrowing of the airways; beta-blockers can trigger severe attacks.
glossary.Beta-agonist: An inhaler drug such as salbutamol that opens the airways by stimulating beta receptors.
glossary.Modified-release: A tablet that releases the drug slowly over many hours.
glossary.Nifedipine: A dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that relaxes arteries.
glossary.Amlodipine: A long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker.
glossary.AV conduction: Passage of the heart's electrical signal from the atria to the ventricles through the AV node.
glossary.AV node: The relay point that passes the electrical signal from the atria to the ventricles.
glossary.Bradycardia: Heart rate below 60 beats per minute.
glossary.Complete heart block: No atrial signals reach the ventricles, which beat slowly on their own.
glossary.Flushing: Sudden reddening and warmth of the skin.
glossary.Anal ulceration: Painful sores around the anus; a side effect of nicorandil.
glossary.Asymmetric dosing: Giving doses at uneven times so there is a long gap with no drug, preventing tolerance.
glossary.Nitrate-free interval: A daily drug-free gap, usually overnight, that stops nitrate tolerance.
glossary.ISMN: Isosorbide mononitrate: a long-acting nitrate tablet.
glossary.Coronary flow reserve: How much coronary blood flow can rise above resting levels when demand increases.
glossary.Contractility: How forcefully the heart muscle squeezes.
glossary.Myocardial oxygen demand: How much oxygen the heart muscle needs; rises with heart rate, BP and contractility.
glossary.Diastolic filling time: The time the heart relaxes and fills; the coronary arteries fill mainly then.
glossary.Diastole: The relaxation phase of the heartbeat.
glossary.LDL: Low-density lipoprotein: 'bad' cholesterol that builds up in plaques.
glossary.Thrombotic: Caused by a blood clot (thrombus) forming in a vessel.
glossary.Demand-supply mismatch: When the heart needs more oxygen than the narrowed arteries can deliver.
